**2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup** — a `verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM before its rows are checked prints no step line and no summary, only the `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` pair last on stderr. It exits 1, and the pair is pinned by the stop table in `tests/cli_verify.rs`. Its stop path adds no time bound: its waits end at the stop, and its kill and pump join end at once. This entry is the source of the picked rows contract/interrupted-verify/exit, contract/interrupted-verify/stderr and contract/viola-verify/interrupted-pair. Part B's test kills the tied stamping `viola verify`, and that test must not contradict them: a SIGKILL is not the Ctrl-C/TERM stop path, so the pair is not expected there. Any TERM-based witness reads the pair.

body: The supply-chain CI job, one job of the GitHub Actions push/PR workflow, must read green on the chunk's own pushed sha with the whole run green; a red job fails the build.
The CI test gate stays whole: no test skipped, ignored or filtered out to make the run green, and no skip or allow entry added by the way.
The in-test boots of the end-to-end harness-lifecycle and cli suites become tied, so a booted wrapper and its fake agent end with their test, killed or not.
A new test kills the tied stamping viola verify and proves nothing of it is left running; it kills only a process it owns and leaves nothing running after it.
Every test that waits on a channel or a thread takes a time bound under the project's 20 s lint; time bounds fall on the driver and the test, never on a human.
Tests must be deterministic: zero flakiness, no retries, every acceptance predicate one that can fail, and every test filter checked to select at least one test.
Failures of the new and changed tests surface as ordinary nextest failures inside the existing test suites, with no separate driver, suite value or artifact of their own.
The killed viola verify is a kill, not an interrupt: the test reads the process census, not the interrupted-verify stderr pair or exit code, and asserts no output of the killed process.
No live claude start in any test: boots use the fake agent, and the test socket goes under the short /tmp root.
The gate's coverage and doctest requirements still hold over the changed and new test code.

A new test kills the tied stamping viola verify and reads, through the process census the last chunk built, that nothing of it is left running; the verify run it kills is one it booted itself.
No test sends a kill at a process it does not own: every kill targets only a process the test spawned and identified, and the proof leaves nothing running after it.
A site sweep for the tie runs over every spelling of a constant, so no untied in-test boot is left under another spelling.

Verify probe directories and captures left by a killed verify run: what verify creates in its own directory must not outlive the killed test, the drop-guard cleanup and the confinement of probe effects to its own directory holding when the process is killed rather than dropped.
Test-side removal only of directories the test created, under its own home and e2e home, following only a safe linked base; viola never touches the e2e-home backing.
A test socket goes under the short per-test root under /tmp, never a Unix socket at the temp root itself; the per-user owner-only socket directory rules hold for booted wrappers in tests.
Every test that waits on a channel or a thread takes a bound under the project's 20 s lint.
Booted wrappers run the fake agent, never the real claude CLI: no live claude start in this chunk and none in CI, and no mutation run.
Test seams the new or changed tests use stay under the fake-agent test-only feature, compiled out of the release build; no new seam forces a security refusal.
The v2-37 ledger note, verified for its named witnesses only, is closed by a claim never weaker than its text: the booted e2e tests and the stamping verify are the witnesses this chunk adds.
Every control the plan fires names its timeout and fires with it, its id within 16 characters, and every test filter it uses is checked to select at least one test.
